editorial:
Imagine being a lonely teenager in the 1930s with no family and nowhere to go, only to be taken under the wing of a scary but powerful mob boss. That is exactly what happens to Billy, a kid who accidentally gets mixed up with the famous gangster Dutch Schultz. You get to see the world through Billy's eyes as he learns how the crime business works and falls for a girl along the way. The vibe is a classic old-school crime story where you feel the tension building as the young boy realizes that his new mentor is actually a loose cannon who can't be trusted.

What really makes this one work is the acting, especially the way the adults treat Billy like a tool rather than a person. The pacing is steady, though it feels more like a character study than a loud action movie. If you like stories about loyalty and betrayal, you will love this. Since it is an older flick, you should try to find a high-quality version to enjoy the period costumes. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture.
endingExplained: As the story wraps up, Dutch Schultz becomes too unstable and paranoid, leading the police to finally close in on him. Billy realizes that Dutch is a monster and decides to help the authorities. After Dutch is killed in a shootout with the cops, Billy is finally free from the gang's grip. He ends up leaving the criminal life behind to start over, having learned a hard lesson about power and greed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic gangster stories and stories about kids growing up too fast.
